investigations.summary: PMM-T2534 (mysqlSlowlogChangeAgent.spec.ts, added by #1760 the day before) failed in all 8 Percona Server compat lanes on pmm-client 3.8.0/3.8.1 with 'unknown flag --skip-connection-check': the flag shipped in 3.9.0 (absent at percona/pmm v3.8.1), and the test had no version gate. It passed in all 3.9.0 lanes, reproduced on a CHAOS VM with 3.8.1, failed again in every 3.8.x lane on re-run, and the fix gates it at 3.9.0 (verified skipped on the VM).

Percona Server 9.7 (latest client): PMM-T2528's slowlog-agent disable was lost to the PMM-15835 status-report race ('Done (disabled)' never reported), and the spec's beforeAll then read agent IDs from shifted pmm-admin list columns ('(disabled)'), so T2529-T2541 failed too. Already covered by open pmm-qa#1778 (agent IDs from pmm-admin list --json plus a finally re-enable); the re-run was green (50 passed, job 133794781399). Deduped, not re-reproduced.

3.10.0 · Percona Server 8.0: T2541 itself passed, but the spec file's afterAll (docker restart + relaunch pmm-agent) never got pmm-agent back on :7777 within 120 s, so all 21 perconaMySqlServer tests after it failed with 'connection refused'. The other 3.10.0 PS lanes passed, the CI artifact holds no in-container pmm-agent log to explain it, and the re-run passed 50/50 (2 skipped).

3.8.1 · PXC 8.4: PMM-T2222 (proxySql.spec.ts) didn't find 'timeout=4' in the container's pmm-agent log after a fixed 2 s sleep. It passed in the other 19 PXC lanes, 13/13 on a CHAOS VM with the 3.8.1 client (5 idle, 8 under full CPU load), and on the re-run (12 passed). A fixed sleep before a one-shot log grep is still a timing weakness worth replacing with polling.

Upgrade 3.6.0 · UI: PMM-T2185 (RTA sort by Host) failed all 3 attempts because rs102's RTA session came back SESSION_STATUS_DOWN from sessions:start (rs101 RUNNING), so only rs101 'hello' queries arrived (trace network). pmm-managed logged no matching error. It passed in every other upgrade lane and on nights 106/107, and the re-run passed T2185 first try.
